plans.note: Section 7 is captioned 'Limitations of Liability' — check whether the cap is mutual, whether it is a meaningful amount tied to fees paid, and whether carve-outs (IP indemnity, confidentiality, gross negligence/willful misconduct) survive the cap. Heading pairing with indemnification of Contractor suggests a vendor-favourable construct.

Section 7 expressly indemnifies the Contractor, i.e. runs against us. Look for any reciprocal Contractor indemnity for third-party IP infringement and its own misconduct (possibly tucked into the warranty section 5); if none exists the rule is unmet on the vendor side while our indemnity is over-broad.

No restrictive covenants section in the outline; scan the purpose/engagement scope (sec-1) and termination (sec-6) for any residual restriction on the businesses we may operate or products we may build.
Check the purpose of engagement clause for exclusive-provider or sole-source language; nothing else in the outline suggests an exclusivity covenant.
Pricing lives in Contractor's Compensation; verify there is no most-favoured-customer obligation running against us. MFN in our favour would be acceptable and not flagged.
Consulting agreements often place a no-hire of Contractor personnel near termination; if present, confirm it is time-limited and carves out general advertising.
Section 6 is the termination clause — confirm we hold a convenience right on reasonable notice with no penalty or acceleration, and that the Contractor cannot terminate at will mid-engagement.
Term/renewal mechanics may sit in the unnumbered term provisions or in sec-6; check for auto-renewal, the non-renewal notice window and any uncapped renewal price uplift.
No general/miscellaneous section appears in the outline; check the tail of sec-7 and the preamble recitals for governing law, venue or arbitration. Flag as missing only if truly absent.
No assignment section listed; look for assignment/change-of-control language at the end of the termination section, including any Contractor right to terminate on our change of control.

Section 4 governs ownership of materials and acceptance — confirm work product vests in us on creation (or by present assignment), that our pre-existing IP and data are untouched, and that acceptance is not conditioned on payment in a way that defers title.

Any licence-back or licence of Contractor background/tools should sit in sec-4; verify it extends to our affiliates and contractors, is perpetual/irrevocable for delivered work, and is not revocable at will.
No audit section listed; check the compensation clause for records inspection rights running against us (frequency, notice, cost allocation).
Scan compensation and liability sections for late-payment penalties, kill fees or liquidated damages payable by us; service credits in our favour are not flagged.

Section 5 contains both the Contractor's warranties and a disclaimer — assess whether the Services warranty against the Specifications runs for a meaningful period with a re-perform/refund remedy, and whether the disclaimer swallows it.

No insurance section in the outline; if the Contractor's personnel touch our systems or premises, an insurance covenant is likely missing and should be added near the reps/warranties or liability provisions.
Check the compensation clause for minimum fees, guaranteed hours or take-or-pay commitments without an exit; scope statement in sec-1 may also fix a committed volume.
Look for post-termination effects in sec-6 (return of materials) and sec-4 (delivery of work product); if there is no transition assistance or data/materials return obligation, treat as missing.
